hero.alt: Dark green title card reading Does Passing Wind Break Wudu?

sources.title: Jami at-Tirmidhi 74: no wudu except for a sound or a smell
sources.supports: Hadith that wudu is required for wind (sound or smell); graded hasan sahih by Tirmidhi.

sources.title: Jami at-Tirmidhi 75: do not leave until hearing a sound or smelling
sources.supports: Hadith on feeling wind in the masjid; Tirmidhi's note on scholars' view and Ibn al-Mubarak on doubt.

sources.title: Sahih al-Bukhari 137: doubt about passing wind in prayer
sources.supports: One who imagines passing wind should not leave prayer unless he hears sound or smells something.

sources.title: Sahih al-Bukhari 177: one should not leave prayer unless he hears sound or smells
sources.supports: Parallel narration of the certainty principle.

sources.title: Darul Ifta Birmingham: Passing Wind
sources.supports: Hanafi ruling: exits from both passages nullify wudu except air from a woman's front passage; certainty without sound or smell breaks wudu; doubt does not.

sources.title: Qur'an 5:6 (Al-Ma'idah)
sources.supports: Relieving oneself among the things requiring purification before prayer.

sources.title: Sunan Abi Dawud 205: breaking wind during prayer
sources.supports: Narration to leave, perform wudu and repeat the prayer; graded Da'if by al-Albani.

review.notes: Re-read each retrieved page text captured 2026-10-27: Tirmidhi 74 and 75, Bukhari 137 and 177, Abu Dawud 205 (Da'if per al-Albani, cited only with that grade), Qur'an 5:6 and Darul Ifta Birmingham 'Passing Wind'. Bukhari 135, Muslim 360/362a and Bukhari 228 returned 403 and are not cited; the 'prayer not accepted' hadith is attributed via the Birmingham page that quotes it. Front-passage exception attributed to the Hanafi school only; no claim about other schools. Continuous-excuse case is only referred to a scholar without a ruling. Hero inspected: 1200x630 forest-palette title card, not duplicated in body. No app CTA; links /prayer-times and existing wudu guides.

claim_checks.claim: There is no Wudu except for a sound or a smell; graded hasan sahih
claim_checks.explanation: Abu Hurairah narrated: 'There no Wudu except for a sound or a smell.' Abu Eisa: hasan sahih.

claim_checks.claim: Man who imagined passing wind in prayer should not leave unless he hears sound or smells something
claim_checks.explanation: Abbad bin Tamim's uncle asked; reply: 'He should not leave his prayers unless he hears sound or smells something.'
'One should not leave his prayer unless he hears sound or smells something.'

claim_checks.claim: Feeling wind in the masjid: do not go out until hearing a sound or smelling; scholars' view and Ibn al-Mubarak on doubt
claim_checks.explanation: Hadith text plus Tirmidhi: scholars hold wudu not obligatory except from a hadath heard or smelled; Ibn al-Mubarak: if in doubt, wudu not required until certain.

claim_checks.claim: Exits from front or back passage nullify wudu except air from a woman's front passage (Hanafi, Raddul Muhtar)
claim_checks.explanation: 'Anything that exists from the front and back passage nullifies wudu except the air, which comes out from the front passage (of a female).'

claim_checks.claim: Certain passing of even small gas breaks wudu without sound or smell; prayer not accepted after breaking wind until wudu
claim_checks.explanation: Cites Fatawa Hindiyyah and Fathul Bari on certainty, and quotes the Bukhari hadith on prayer not accepted until wudu.

claim_checks.claim: Relieving oneself is among things requiring purification before prayer
claim_checks.explanation: Verse: 'or have relieved yourselves ... then purify yourselves'.

claim_checks.claim: Abu Dawud narration to leave, perform wudu and repeat prayer is graded weak by al-Albani
claim_checks.explanation: Text: 'he should turn away and perform ablution and repeat the prayer.' Grade: Da'if (Al-Albani).
